Package io.mavlink4j.service

Class HeartbeatService

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.service.HeartbeatService
public final class HeartbeatService extends Object
MAVLink's heartbeat microservice (Family B — streaming, see docs/API.md): emits our own HEARTBEAT at a fixed rate, and tracks each known peer's connected/disconnected state against peerTimeout (convention "4-5 missed heartbeats" — not a spec number).

Which links get our heartbeat

Built from PeerDirectory + FrameSink only (the L4 role interfaces) — there is no "list every registered link" seam at this level. Each tick derives its broadcast targets from the distinct Peer.link() values currently known to PeerDirectory: this service's heartbeat reaches every link something has already been heard on. A dial-out link with a fixed destination that has never sent us anything is not reachable this way. That is an accepted, documented gap rather than an oversight (and, for a listen-style link, costs nothing: MavlinkLink#send cannot address an unlearned target at all, so nothing was reachable there either).

Connectivity tracking is this class's own, not LinkHealth's

LinkHealth is deliberately not one of L4's small role interfaces (the four are FrameSink, Correlator, PeerDirectory, TxScheduler) — it stays a session-level protocol-accounting concern. This class computes its own connected/disconnected view straight from Peer.lastHeard() vs. peerTimeout, independently, on every tick.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the periodic emit. Idempotent — a second call while already started is a no-op.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the periodic emit. Idempotent.

    • isConnected

      public boolean isConnected(PeerId id)
      true if id was heard within peerTimeout as of the most recent tick; false for a disconnected or never-known peer. Reflects only what has been observed as of the last tick, not a live "now" recomputation — matches how start() drives this service's own notion of time.
